clue.text: Medicine provided is about to give a lift

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so both pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine
provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'

explanation.surface: A pharmacist claims the medicine will cheer the patient up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' turns the whole run PILL + IF backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a boost or stimulus, something that raises the spirits.

clue.text: Run through motorway, climbing barrier

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the piece is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: MI stands for the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway
a pale is a fence stake, so a barrier

explanation.surface: A runner crosses a motorway by climbing over the barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce through with something pointed.

clue.text: Not the main sort of crustacean

definitions.text: Not the main sort of crustacean

parts.words: Not the main sort of crustacean
parts.note: the main is the sea, so this is a crustacean of dry ground rather than the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: These crabs live mostly ashore, returning to water only to breed.

clue.text: Place with a disease hard to eradicate for this odd creature

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for Place in addresses

indicators.note: to eradicate means the hard letter must be wiped out of the disease word

parts.note: typhus is an infectious disease
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A place with an incurable disease breeds a strange animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eradicate' takes H out of TYPHUS, leaving TYPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed, egg-laying Australian mammal is famously strange.

clue.text: With cards held, club lead gives firm control

indicators.note: lead says the club piece goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
a hand is the set of cards a player holds

explanation.surface: A card player holding a good hand leads clubs and dominates the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture misleads: 'club' is a golf club, and 'lead' puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule with an iron hand is to exercise strict, unyielding authority.

clue.text: Divine female's ruling over state

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the ruling piece above the goddess

parts.note: in means in power, ruling
Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt

explanation.surface: A goddess holds sway over a whole territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a US state in the Midwest.

clue.text: Old pet Noah destroyed? No way!

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Noah's elderly pet perished: there was no saving it.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation saying there is no chance at all of success.

clue.text: A revolutionary plan upsetting the world of learning

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue turns the plan word upside down, so backwards

parts.note: an aim is a plan

explanation.surface: A rebel's scheme threatens to overturn the universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the scholarly community of universities.

clue.text: Well below the surface, like Neptune, perhaps

definitions.meaning: firmly established, hard to dig out
Neptune, the Roman sea god, sits on a throne in the deep ocean

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: seated in the deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-rooted feelings lie far beneath the surface, and a sea god is seated in the deep.

clue.text: European resort over Channel

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: over signals turning the channel word back to front

parts.note: a drain is a channel for water

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses the Channel to reach a resort on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DRAIN into NIARD. 'Channel' looks like the English Channel but is just a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a native of Spain, a European country.

clue.text: Attack, in a way, by fliers at start of engagement

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is made up of fliers

indicators.note: only the opening letter of engagement is taken

explanation.surface: Airmen launch an attack at the very start of a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: A wealth I lost in sly behaviour

indicators.note: lost tells us the letter I goes missing from the word for wealth

parts.note: richness means wealth

explanation.surface: Someone who lost their fortune turned to cunning ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes the I out of RICHNESS, leaving RCHNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Archness is knowing slyness or mischievous cunning in manner.

clue.text: Swimmer quietly coming in to land

indicators.note: coming in to says the quiet letter enters the land word

parts.note: terrain is land
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A swimmer silently comes ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, which swims.

clue.text: It indicates the precise moment daily one churchman turns up

parts.note: The Times is a British daily newspaper
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the churchman is read bottom to top

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1930s

explanation.surface: A clergyman appears every day at exactly the same moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reads LANG upwards as GNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The pips broadcast on radio mark the exact hour.

clue.text: A couple of doctors like a port on the Indian Ocean

definitions.text: a port on the Indian Ocean

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, one doctor
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a second doctor
as means like

explanation.surface: Two doctors compare something to a seaport in East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Mombasa is Kenya's main seaport, on the Indian Ocean coast.

clue.text: Become tarnished under cloud of suspicion

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the tarnishing word beneath the cloud

parts.note: mist is a cloud of fine droplets
to rust is to corrode, become tarnished

explanation.surface: Someone's reputation is tarnished when they come under suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistrust is a lack of trust, doubt about someone.

clue.text: Mishap I had contracted, beset by stress

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the short form sits inside the stress word

parts.note: an accent is stress on a syllable
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A patient blames a mishap on an illness caught under stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' suggests catching an illness but signals the short form I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unfortunate unplanned event.

clue.text: A gentle model exhibiting style

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A gentle fashion model shows off her style on the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a catwalk model but is the anagram signal for A GENTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful and stylish in appearance or manner.

clue.text: Emergency equipment gets passenger up into hoist

indicators.note: into says the reversed passenger goes inside the hoist word

parts.note: a lift is a hoist

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the passenger word is read upwards

parts.note: a fare is a paying passenger

explanation.surface: A passenger is winched up into a hoist during a rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable boat carried for abandoning ship is safety gear.

clue.text: Cracked up latest support for travel

indicators.note: support for in a down clue puts the latest word beneath the travel word

parts.note: to go is to travel
newest means latest

explanation.surface: The newest walking frame has cracked under the strain of travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken or ruined is said to have died or been lost.

clue.text: Letters distributed in support of Board

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Letters are handed out in backing of the company board.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame holding up a tabletop.

clue.text: Money dropped in long grass is returned

indicators.note: dropped in says the money is placed inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a fund is a sum of money

explanation.surface: Cash dropped in tall grass is handed back to its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that has been paid back has been repaid.

clue.text: Inventor's team up and running

definitions.note: read as 'Inventor is', the 's a link

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the team word is read upwards

parts.note: a side is a team
on means running, as a machine

explanation.surface: An inventor's team is up and running.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison invented the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Rueing it when involved in conspiracy

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A plotter regrets getting drawn into a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrigue is secret plotting or scheming.

clue.text: Ill-feeling caused by new drivers holding practice

indicators.note: holding says the drivers' letters go around the practice word

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation for drivers
use means practice or custom

explanation.surface: Learner drivers get queasy during their practice sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' suggests resentment, but here it is literal sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is a sick feeling in the stomach.

clue.text: Partygoers restricted by time limits getting cross

indicators.note: restricted by means the partygoers are hemmed in by the other piece
limits are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of time

parts.note: ravers are people who go to wild parties

explanation.surface: Revellers get angry when made to leave by a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs over a column break on the page. 'cross' looks like 'angry' but means to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across something.

clue.text: Commonplace opening dropped in play

indicators.note: opening dropped means the first letter of the word for commonplace is removed

parts.note: a platitude is a commonplace remark

explanation.surface: A trite opening line is cut from a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a drama but means room to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is freedom of action, as with play in a rope.

clue.text: Carrying the can, got put back outside

indicators.note: outside says the reversed piece goes around the can word
put back signals that the word got is reversed

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone who carried the can for others was pushed outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' gives TOG, which wraps round TIN. 'Carrying the can' is an idiom for taking the blame, but 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Toting means carrying or lugging something around.
